positive.prompt: Prove that docking works with an ordinary terminal, using the smallest real experiment
Before building the prototype, test whether this uncertain capability is feasible on the actual desktop
Run a bounded technical spike for a proof of concept, without preparing a special target

negative.prompt: Compare two retrieval approaches on the same data and report the tradeoffs
The app worked yesterday but now crashes on startup. Find the root cause and fix the bug.

evals.prompt: Use claim.md and observations.json to assess this feasibility experiment. Produce report.html and a minimal next experiment record. Do not launch services, access a real desktop, or change the agreed claim. Identify whether the observations answer it and what evidence is missing.
evals.expected_output: An evidence-bound assessment that rejects prepared-target success as proof of ordinary-terminal adoption, reports missing real-surface evidence and defines the smallest valid next test.
expectations: The report retains ordinary independently opened terminals as a required condition, rather than accepting the specially launched window as equivalent
The original claim is not marked supported or complete because a helper receipt reports success
The report distinguishes a successful managed-window operation from unproved external-terminal adoption
The next test includes a real ordinary terminal and a known-different target, with a stopping rule and evidence requirement
No services or live desktop operations are launched and no source observations are rewritten
